subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and what is the first supported milestone?
rationale: The next step requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, and migration boundaries that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, and per-agent lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat #82017 and #84758 as the current scope and leave the broader Gateway/control-plane split deferred until the placement contract is reviewed.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Keep supporting multi-gateway and operator workarounds without committing to a distributed runtime boundary now.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, and per-agent lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest current-main history signal for the inspected Gateway and agent runtime surfaces and the author of the related worker-runtime experiment.
